summary: iter-140.g verification (backend + frontend). Backend: wrote an INDEPENDENT 25-case review suite (/app/backend/tests/test_iter140g_review.py) for POST /api/admin/factory-reset and POST /api/admin/users/{id}/wallet-adjust — 25/25 pass. Covered: unauth 401/403, non-admin 403 (both apply and dry_run), missing/wrong confirm -> 400 with 'YES-DELETE-ALL' hint, dry_run shape (would_reset_users / would_delete_txns == live txn count / total_deducted_after_reset) + byte-for-byte DB purity, apply semantics on 5 seeded shapes (8-days-old sub -> meals_used=16, wallet=2800-8*93.33=2053.36, end=start+30, paused_days=0, user_paused=false, scan_deducted_dates={}, last_tick_date=today-1; today-start sub -> full 2800/0 meals; 40-days-old sub -> status='expired', meals_used capped at 60, wallet floored; orphan user and expired-sub-only user zeroed to 0.0; pre-expired subs untouched), whole-ledger wipe (0 non-factory_reset rows survive), exactly ONE kind='factory_reset' audit row per reseeded sub with actor_user_id, users.wallet_balance synced to sub wallet, and full idempotency on a second apply. Wallet-adjust no-snap: +465 on a 30d/Rs.2800 sub -> auto_derived {days:5, meals:10, snapped_delta:465.0, residue:0.0}, user AND sub wallet exactly 3265.00, meals_total 60->70 with meals_used untouched, end_date +5d; -465 reverses exactly (wallet back to 2800, end_date -5d, meals_used 0->10); Rs.20 (<1 day) derives 0 days and only moves the wallet; explicit extend_days disables auto-derive; incomplete profile -> 400; blank reason -> 400; non-admin -> 403. Also re-ran the dev's suites (test_iter140g_factory_reset.py, test_iter140b_refund_review.py, test_iter140_double_deduct.py) against the PUBLIC preview URL: 33/33 pass. Frontend /admin/users (cookie-seeded admin session): factory-reset-panel renders, Preview opens factory-reset-modal with '2 sub(s) will be reseeded / Deletes 2 wallet transactions / Rs.559.98 total will be deducted', Apply is disabled empty and with 'yes-delete-all' (case-sensitive gate works) and enables only on exact 'YES-DELETE-ALL', Cancel closes with no side effects and clears the phrase on reopen, and the real apply produced the toast 'Reset 2 subs · deleted 2 txns · deducted Rs.559.98' with the DB verified (victim sub wallet 400->2240.02, meals_used 33->12, junk ledger row gone, user wallet synced to 2240.02). No console errors other than a pre-existing 'Provider's accounts list is empty.' warning.

minor.issue: Non-atomic destructive sequence: the whole wallet_transactions collection is deleted FIRST, then each sub is rewritten in a per-document Python loop, then every users doc is updated one-by-one. A crash/timeout mid-run leaves the ledger wiped with subs partly reseeded and no rollback. Use bulk_write / updateMany (and consider a Mongo transaction or a pre-write snapshot dump) — on a production-sized DB the per-doc loop over db.users.find({}) is also O(N) round-trips.

Audit row is written as type='credit' with amount = the REMAINING wallet balance (not an actual credit event). Any report that reconstructs a balance by summing ledger credits/debits will now be wrong. Suggest kind-specific type (e.g. 'adjustment') or amount=0 with the balance only in balance_after.

meals_total is preserved rather than normalised to 60. If a sub had been extended by a wallet-adjust (meals_total 70), the reset restores wallet=plan_amount (2800) while leaving 70 meals -> wallet/meals invariant broken and the admin's earlier paid extension silently survives the 'nuclear' reset while its money does not. Spec said meals_total=60.
wallet_balance is zeroed for EVERY users document (admins, staff, franchise owners included), not just role='subscriber'. Works as spec'd but is broader than 'users with no active sub'.

Response key is still named auto_derived.snapped_delta and residue is hard-coded 0.0 even though nothing is snapped anymore. With +465 at Rs.93.33/day the wallet gets 465 but 5 days/10 meals worth Rs.466.65 are granted — a real Rs.1.65 under-funding that residue=0 hides. Rename to applied_delta and (optionally) report the true derived_value - delta gap for audit clarity.

Asymmetric meals accounting: positive delta bumps meals_total, negative delta bumps meals_used. A +465 then -465 round trip returns wallet/end_date exactly but leaves meals_total=70 and meals_used=10 instead of 60/0 — meals_left is correct (60) yet the historical counters are permanently inflated.

design_issues.screen: Admin > Users & Roles — Danger zone factory reset
issues: A mistyped phrase gives no inline feedback: the Apply button just stays disabled (the toast.warning path in applyFactoryReset is unreachable because the button is disabled unless the phrase matches). A short 'phrase does not match' hint under the input would help.
The modal has no Escape-key / backdrop-click close and no focus trap — only the Cancel button closes it.

Preview button label flips to 'Scanning…' for the whole panel state (shared `resetting` flag also drives the Apply button label), acceptable but the panel has no post-apply summary of who was reseeded even though the API returns a `sample` array.

action_items: Make factory-reset atomic-ish: bulk_write the sub reseeds + a single updateMany to zero user wallets before applying per-user totals, so a mid-run failure can't leave the ledger wiped with subs unreseeded.
Stop writing the reset audit row as type='credit' with amount = remaining balance (breaks ledger-sum reconciliation).
Decide meals_total policy on reset: normalise to 60 (per spec) or explicitly document that admin-extended meals survive a factory reset while the wallet does not.
Rename auto_derived.snapped_delta -> applied_delta and surface the real (days*per_day - delta) gap instead of a hard-coded residue=0.
Optional UI: inline 'phrase does not match' hint + Escape/backdrop close on the factory-reset modal; render the API's `sample` list after apply.
critical_code_review_comments: admin_factory_reset deletes ALL wallet_transactions before any sub is rewritten and does one update_one per sub and per user — no atomicity and O(N) round-trips; use bulk_write/updateMany and write the audit rows before/with the reseed.
The factory_reset ledger row records type='credit' amount=<remaining wallet>, which is not an economic event and will corrupt any sum-based balance reconstruction.

meals_total is carried over from the pre-reset sub, so a previously extended plan keeps its extra meals while its wallet is reset to plan_amount — wallet ~= meals_left * per_meal invariant is broken after a reset.
wallet-adjust auto_derive now grants 5 days/10 meals for Rs.465 (worth Rs.466.65) and reports residue=0.0 — the residue field is now dishonest; the 'snapped_delta' key name is also stale.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (panel render, preview modal figures, typed-confirm gating, cancel, real apply + toast + DB verification)

context_for_next_testing_agent: IMPORTANT: /api/admin/factory-reset is GLOBAL and destructive — every run during this iteration wiped the preview DB's wallet_transactions and reseeded ALL active subs (preview DB currently holds only ~2 active subs and 1 factory_reset ledger row). Snapshot before running it. Regression suites: /app/backend/tests/test_iter140g_review.py (25 cases, ordered — factory-reset classes must run BEFORE the wallet-adjust class, use -p no:randomly) and /app/backend/tests/test_iter140g_factory_reset.py. The dev suite defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8001/api; override with EFC_API_URL to hit the public preview URL. For the AdminUsers UI, seed a cookie session with /app/test_reports/seed_iter142_ui.py.
rca_of_the_issue: Both iter-140.g changes verified effective. (1) Snapping removal: the auto-derive block now sets explicit_extend = round(delta/per_day) and meals_change = days*2 while leaving `delta` untouched, so the wallet moves by the exact typed rupees (3265.00, not 3266.65) and residue is 0 by construction; the trade-off is that the wallet is now Rs.1.65 short of the value of the days/meals granted, which is intentional per the admin's request. (2) Factory reset reseeds off sub.start_date (not end_date), so days_elapsed = (IST today - start_date) capped at 30 drives both the wallet deduction (per_day * days) and meals_used (2 * days, capped at meals_total), with last_tick_date = today-1 preventing the midnight tick from re-charging those days — hence the observed idempotency across repeat runs. Remaining risks are operational (non-atomic wipe-then-rewrite, misleading audit row semantics, meals_total carry-over), not functional.
